Pilot Sample Size for a Bounded Length Confidence Interval for a Median, Distribution Free

Source: R/seq_blci_dfr_median.R
seq_blci_dfr_median_pilot.Rd

Returns the number of observations to collect before the stopping rule of seq_blci_dfr_median is checked for the first time. That procedure is the purely sequential bounded length confidence interval for the median of a population whose distribution is not specified (Mukhopadhyay and de Silva, 2009).

Usage

seq_blci_dfr_median_pilot(d, conf_level = 0.95, m_0 = 10, gamma = 1)

Arguments

d

Half of the largest interval length allowed, in the units of the data: sampling continues until the length of the interval is at most \(2d\). A positive number.

conf_level

The confidence level (default 0.95).

m_0

The smallest pilot sample size allowed, in addition to the minimum the confidence level itself requires. A whole number of at least 2; default 10.

gamma

Positive constant that sets how fast the pilot grows as the target narrows; see Details. Default 1.

Value

A length one integer giving the pilot sample size.

Details

The pilot is the largest of three numbers: $$m = \max\{n_{\min},\ m_0,\ \lceil (z_{\alpha/2}/d)^{2/(1 + \gamma)} \rceil\}.$$ The first, \(n_{\min}\), is the smallest sample size at which an interval formed from order statistics can reach the confidence level at all. The widest such interval, from the smallest to the largest observation, misses the median only when every observation falls on the same side of it, so its coverage is \(1 - 2^{1-n}\); \(n_{\min}\) is the smallest \(n\) for which this is at least conf_level (5, 6, and 8 observations at 90%, 95%, and 99%).

The third is of lower order than the sample size the procedure will need, which is approximately \(n^* = (z_{\alpha/2}/d)^2 / \{4 f(\theta)^2\}\) for a population with density \(f\) at its median \(\theta\). The density is unknown before sampling, so the pilot uses only the known constant \((z_{\alpha/2}/d)^2\); with the default \(\gamma = 1\) the third term is \(\lceil z_{\alpha/2}/d \rceil\). A pilot equal to \((z_{\alpha/2}/d)^2\) itself would be several times too large for a population that is concentrated near its median in the units of the data.

This is the package's pilot rule, of the same form as the pilot sample size of Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2018, Equation 21). It should not be read as the pilot size prescribed by Mukhopadhyay and de Silva (2009).

References

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2018). Accuracy in parameter estimation for a general class of effect sizes: A sequential approach. Psychological Methods, 23(2), 226–243. doi:10.1037/met0000127

Mukhopadhyay, N., & de Silva, B. M. (2009). Sequential methods and their applications. Chapman & Hall/CRC. ISBN:9780367386535

See also

seq_blci_dfr_median

Other seq_blci_dfr_median: seq_blci_dfr_median()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# Median household income (thousands of dollars), interval no longer
# than 10 thousand
seq_blci_dfr_median_pilot(d = 5, conf_level = 0.95)
#> [1] 10
# A tight target and a high confidence level
seq_blci_dfr_median_pilot(d = 0.1, conf_level = 0.99)
#> [1] 26
